A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CABLD and provide readable main text and complete supplementary material. Equations, tables, figures, and relocated passages can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v2 reports original landmark-detection experiments, ablations, rotation and age analyses, and Parkinson’s and Alzheimer’s disease classification results.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds template-sensitivity, pathological-brain accuracy, and inference-time results.

M1.justification: The landmark network, registration and consistency losses, adaptive loss schedule, TPS transformation, and random-convolution augmentation are unchanged. Colin27 is tested as an alternative reference within the existing method.

E1.justification: Supplementary Section 6 adds direct landmark evaluation on 36 LHSCPD Parkinson’s patients with 1.5T gadolinium-enhanced T1w scans. This extends the existing brain-MRI coverage to a pathological cohort with additional contrast and acquisition shifts; previous benchmarks and diagnostic tasks remain.

E2.justification: Existing accuracy and rotation comparisons retain their comparator sets. New focused comparisons evaluate Colin27-based CABLD against KeyMorph with 512 keypoints and ICBM152, and compare inference times against ANTs (MI/CC), KeyMorph, and BrainMorph. These reuse existing algorithms in additional comparisons.

E3.justification: v3 adds evaluation using Colin27, compares pathological-brain accuracy with the existing healthy 40–90-year age range, and introduces CPU/GPU inference-time measurements. The original preprocessing, training budget, accuracy metrics, and benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 assesses age-related template effects but leaves alternative atlases for future work and evaluates pathology indirectly through diagnosis. v3 adds actual alternative-template sensitivity and direct pathological-brain/domain-shift testing, substantially extending validation of template dependence and clinical applicability.

E5.justification: Both versions already report plus/minus summaries, significance tests, and cross-validation results. The additions continue these reporting practices without introducing seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or a newly specified statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3, existing figures, and diagnostic scores are unchanged. Supplementary Sections 5–7 add four Colin27 accuracy results, LHSCPD MRE of 5.19 ± 2.13 mm, and comparative inference times, including CABLD’s 0.35 ± 0.012 s on GPU and 6.42 ± 0.20 s on CPU. These introduce findings on template sensitivity, pathological-brain accuracy, and efficiency.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations 1–8 and S1–S6 are unchanged. The TPS derivation is relocated and its section renumbered without mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about single-reference annotation, contrast generalization, consistency regularization, accuracy, and clinical applicability. The abstract’s code announcement adds access information.

C2.justification: v3 interprets poorer Colin27 accuracy through single-subject versus population-average template stability and discusses template selection. It also distinguishes indirect diagnostic evidence from direct pathological landmark testing and identifies annotation availability as a constraint on validation for other disorders.

D1.justification: v3 adds a public-code access statement and repository link, and clarifies that the existing Alzheimer’s comparison uses healthy subjects in the same age range. Training implementation details remain unchanged; the new timing section identifies CPU/GPU execution but omits hardware models and measurement repetition details.

R1.justification: v3 adds Holmes et al. on Colin27 and Fonov and Collins on population-template stability to support the new sensitivity discussion. BrainMorph’s reference changes from preprint to publication metadata, while the broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative receives limited wording and terminology edits. Ethics and data acknowledgments move from the supplement into an expanded main acknowledgment, the approving institution is named, and supplementary sections are renumbered and extended.

P2.justification: Table 2 is reduced in display size, and supplementary figures are redistributed among the prose. All seven figures retain identical image content, and the tables retain their entries; these are layout changes rather than new visual evidence.

improvement.justification: v3 replaces promised alternative-atlas testing with measured sensitivity, adds direct accuracy evidence on pathological scans, and provides code-access information. These targeted additions improve validation and transparency while preserving the principal results. The improvement is bounded by the limited new test scenarios and incompletely specified timing measurements.
